title: Mapping global eco-environment vulnerability due to human and nature disturbances
author: Nguyen, Liou

steps.title: Initialize GIS environment
steps.instruction: Create an ArcGIS 10.3 project, set the spatial reference to WGS‑84 (zone 48 N), define a target raster resolution of 0.0833° × 0.0833° (pixel size), which yields approximately 4320 columns by 1673 rows for the global extent, and ensure all layers will be stored as GeoTIFF files.

steps.title: Prepare soil moisture layer
steps.instruction: Retrieve annual average soil moisture from the L‑band SMOS mission (provided by INRA and CESBIO) in NetCDF format, convert to GeoTIFF, mosaic the tiles, classify the raster into eight classes on a 0.25‑degree grid, and interpolate areas with insufficient or shallow‑effect data.

steps.title: Prepare precipitation layer
steps.instruction: Download the global annual average precipitation GeoTIFF (resolution 0.00833°), classify it into eight classes, and interpolate missing values using thin‑plate splines with elevation and distance‑to‑coast as covariates; use weather‑station data from 9 000–60 000 stations covering 1970–2000.

steps.title: Prepare temperature layer
steps.instruction: Obtain the global average temperature GeoTIFF (resolution 0.00833°), classify into eight classes, and process it with the same weather‑station data and thin‑plate spline interpolation method as the precipitation layer.

steps.title: Compute distance from hydrological network
steps.instruction: Load the inland water surface shapefile, run the Euclidean Distance tool in ArcGIS to calculate distance to the network, and classify the resulting raster into eight classes.

steps.title: Process population data
steps.instruction: Import the population Excel file, convert it to a shapefile, re‑export as GeoTIFF, and classify the raster into eight classes.

steps.title: Process income data
steps.instruction: Import the income Excel file, convert to a shapefile, re‑export as GeoTIFF, and classify the raster into five classes.

steps.title: Compute distance from urban areas
steps.instruction: Load the urban‑area shapefile, apply the Euclidean Distance tool in ArcGIS, and classify the distance raster into eight classes ranging from near to far.

steps.title: Process land‑use/land‑cover (LULC)
steps.instruction: Download MODIS Land Cover Type product (MCD12Q1, 2017) in HDF format (500 m SIN Grid), mosaic the tiles, convert to GeoTIFF, and classify into 16 classes according to the provider legend.

steps.title: Process NDVI layer
steps.instruction: Download MODIS 16‑day L3 Global NDVI (500 m), mosaic the tiles, compute the mean NDVI for the year 2017, convert to GeoTIFF, and classify into five classes.

steps.title: Process natural hazard layers
steps.instruction: For each hazard (drought, tropical cyclone, landslide, flood) download the source (Excel, shapefile, or GeoTIFF), convert to GeoTIFF at 0.0833° resolution, resample to match other layers, assign an equal weight of 0.25, aggregate the four rasters by weighted sum in ArcGIS, and classify the final natural‑hazard raster into five classes.

substeps.instruction: Tropical cyclones: download, convert, resample, weight = 0.25.

steps.title: Process DEM layer
steps.instruction: Download SRTM DEM GeoTIFF (resolution 0.00833°), fill any voids, and classify the DEM into eight classes.

steps.title: Process slope‑constraint layer
steps.instruction: Download the slope‑constraint dataset at 0.0833° resolution, convert to GeoTIFF, and classify into eight classes from low to very frequent constraint.

steps.title: Process slope‑aspect layer
steps.instruction: Calculate slope aspect from the SRTM DEM using the ArcGIS slope‑aspect function, convert the result to GeoTIFF, and classify into ten aspect classes.

steps.title: Prepare PM2.5 validation data
steps.instruction: Obtain the annual global PM2.5 map derived from MODIS (references [20, 21]) and keep it as a GeoTIFF for later validation.

steps.title: Derive global weights with AHP
steps.instruction: Gather judgments from five international experts, construct pairwise comparison matrices for the five domains (natural hazards, society‑economics, topography, hydrometeorology, land resources) using the 9‑point Saaty scale, compute the priority vector (global weights: natural hazards 0.395, society‑economics 0.242, topography 0.123, hydrometeorology 0.169, land resources 0.070), calculate λmax, CI, and CR (CR = 0.007 < 0.1 confirming consistency), and record class weights for each indicator as listed in Table 7.

steps.title: Classify indicator layers with Natural Breaks
steps.instruction: Apply the Natural Break (Jenks) statistical classification method in ArcGIS to each indicator raster where required, using the class numbers specified (e.g., eight classes for soil moisture, precipitation, temperature, distance layers, population, DEM, slope‑constraint; five classes for income, NDVI, natural‑hazard composite; sixteen classes for LULC; ten classes for slope aspect).

steps.title: Create weighted overlay vulnerability map
steps.instruction: Overlay all classified indicator rasters in ArcGIS, assigning each the local weight (wj) from Table 7 (e.g., soil moisture 0.384, precipitation 0.300, temperature 0.191, etc.) and the domain global weight (Wi), multiply raster values by their respective weights, sum the weighted rasters to produce the final global eco‑environmental vulnerability map.
